section_summary: This section contains the end of one copy and the beginning of another copy of Yasuo Tatsuki’s 1948 study of Japanese public opinion after the Second World War. The study summarizes surveys on political parties and cabinets, the new constitution, inflation, the planned February 1947 general strike, and revisions to family law. The pages are partly duplicated and some scanned leaves appear out of printed-page order.

subfiles.title: General Trend of Japanese Opinion Following the End of War, concluding pages
subfiles.about: The surviving end of the study reports surveys on the February 1947 general strike, Civil Code reform, and women’s political choices.
subfiles.summary: Survey results show broad disapproval of the proposed strike by public employees, alongside occupational differences in support. The Civil Code section examines abolition of the household system and equality between men and women. A final survey compares husbands’ and wives’ electoral preferences in three communities; the Japanese colophon gives a publication date of May 25, 1948.

subfiles.title: General Trend of Japanese Opinion Following the End of War
subfiles.about: A second copy of Tatsuki’s study compiles postwar Japanese opinion surveys on politics, the economy, labor, and social reform.
subfiles.summary: After its cover, title page, and contents, the study describes Japanese survey methods and reports opinion on the Yoshida and Katayama cabinets, political parties, and proposed constitutional provisions. It then covers inflation and household income, public reaction to the planned February 1947 general strike, and attitudes toward abolishing the household system and establishing equality between men and women. The section ends during a discussion of whether wives followed their husbands’ political preferences.
